consumer: The delivery-quest/mission completion check that the HUD reflects, asking 'is the quest's required item requirement satisfied?' — an engine-computed mission predicate (e.g. mission::is_complete / has_target item-requirement logic), not a raw item enumerator.
scope: The mission requirement's own possession/charge-accounting reach (the engine's has_amount/has_charges/component-match over the avatar's effective inventory, including items nested in worn containers), matching the quest's required scope — not a flat on-person item dump.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — it iterates wielded_items(), worn, and inv_const_slice() and dumps each item's type_id/charges/count_by_charges; it does NOT call any mission/requirement predicate, so 'satisfied' would have to be re-derived from this partial list (a shortcut), and it omits contents nested inside worn containers.
divergence: Quest needs N charges of a charge-counted item (or the required item sits inside a worn container/holster): the engine's mission predicate returns satisfied=true via has_charges/contained-item accounting, but a HUD re-scanning carried_items would miscount charges or never see the contained item and report satisfied=false (or vice-versa).
